segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Sit or lie comfortably. Place a hand on the belly if useful and let several breaths happen without changing them.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice movement beneath the hand. Invite the belly and lower ribs to make a little more room on the next inhale.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Imagine a moonlit accordion beneath the ribs opening easily... then folding home on the exhale.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Keep the breath quiet. The chest may move too; nothing needs to be locked.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Try an easy rhythm: inhale one... two... three... exhale one... two... three... only while comfortable.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] Release counting at the first sign of strain. Ordinary breathing is always available.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel the lower ribs widen to the sides and perhaps slightly into the back.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let the accordion play almost silently for several breaths, with no need for maximum depth.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If dizziness, tingling, or discomfort appears, stop shaping the breath and rest.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice how exhaling can finish without squeezing. Let the folds close by themselves.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Remove the hand if you wish and see whether the body remembers the easy movement.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Release the exercise. Return to natural breathing and the sounds of the room.
